newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Riksbank repeats call for Sweden in EMU at start.
newsitem.headline: Riksbank repeats call for Sweden in EMU at start.

text.p: Sweden's central bank on Tuesday reiterated its support for Sweden to join Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) from the start in 1999, saying Sweden will probably fulfil the convergence criteria.

The Riksbank's deputy governor Stefan Ingves said the possibility for Sweden to influence important decisions was likely to be reduced in other fields beside monetary policy if Sweden stayed outside the euro area.
"As far as Sweden is concerned, it looks as though we will in fact fulfil the convergence criteria," Ingves said in a speech to be given to the Swedish Retail Federation.
"Whether or not we participate will therefore depend on the decision by the Swedish pariament.
"If Sweden were to refrain from joining the euro area at all, there would be a risk of being marginalised as an outsider."
Ingves said common opinion for Sweden's entry to EMU in 1999 appeared to be a soft no.
"A common opinion at present seems to be that a soft no is not unlikely and would not involve appreciably higher economic costs than participation from the start."
"Deferring participation for some years would not exclude us from the euro area for good.

"If we intend to join the euro area in a not-too-distant future after 1999, the recommendation therefore seems to be participate from the start and avoid unnecessary and costly solutions for firms as well as society."
Ingves said the list of countries to be included in the EMU at the January 1 start would not be known until spring 1998.
